$comment: THE source of truth for every environment value Duncit reads.
techPortal: categories + fields the Tech portal manages (envEntry.fields.ts loads this file; labels, hints, descriptions and validation all come from here).
githubSecrets: the only values that stay in GitHub Actions secrets, and why each cannot move to the Tech portal.
usedIn lists are GENERATED: run `node scripts/audit-env-registry.mjs --write` after changing code that reads a value, and commit the result.
alsoReadBy (hand-written, optional): files that build a category's env keys at run time, e.g. SOCIAL_${provider}_${field}, so no literal can be found; they are folded into usedIn.
validation.type is one of: text, url, hostname, email, phone, number, bool, json, pem, list, fingerprints. validation.required is enforced when an entry is created.

SOCIAL_INSTAGRAM.description: Connect Instagram professional accounts through Facebook Login for Business (Unified login); read posts and comments; publish posts and reels

fields.name: app_id
fields.label: Meta App ID
fields.hint: developers.facebook.com/apps → your app → App settings → Basic → App ID. With Unified login this is the Meta app ID, not a separate Instagram app ID
fields.description: Meta app the Instagram button connects accounts through (Facebook Login for Business). Usually the same app as the Facebook entry.

fields.name: app_secret
fields.label: Meta App Secret
fields.hint: Same page → App secret
fields.description: Exchanges the login code for a token and checks granted permissions (debug_token) for Instagram accounts.

fields.name: login_config_id
fields.label: Login configuration ID
fields.hint: developers.facebook.com/apps → your app → Use cases → Instagram API → API setup with Unified login → Facebook Login for Business → Configurations → Configuration ID. The configuration must include the Facebook Page, its Instagram account and the messaging permissions
fields.description: Facebook Login for Business configuration the Instagram button Connect opens. Meta takes the permissions and the asset picker (Pages and Instagram accounts) from it; when empty, Connect asks for the default permission list instead.

fields.name: graph_version
fields.label: Graph API Version (optional)
fields.hint: e.g. v23.0; default v23.0
fields.description: Graph API version every Instagram call on graph.facebook.com is pinned to.

fields.name: webhook_verify_token
fields.label: Webhook verify token
fields.hint: Any long random string you choose. Paste the same value in Meta for Developers → your app → Webhooks (Instagram and Page objects) → Verify token, with the callback URL https://<server>/social/webhooks/meta
fields.description: Proves to Meta that the webhook URL is ours when Meta checks the subscription. Webhooks deliver Instagram and Messenger DMs and comments to the Inbox within seconds; the scheduled sync stays as the fallback.

SOCIAL_FACEBOOK.description: Connect Facebook Pages (and their linked Instagram accounts) through Facebook Login for Business; read posts and comments; publish to Pages

fields.name: app_id
fields.label: Meta App ID
fields.hint: developers.facebook.com/apps → your app → App settings → Basic → App ID. Posting to Pages needs pages_manage_posts under the Pages use case
fields.description: Facebook app Pages are connected through.

fields.name: app_secret
fields.label: Meta App Secret
fields.hint: App settings → Basic → App secret
fields.description: Exchanges the login code for a token and checks granted permissions (debug_token) for Facebook Pages.

fields.name: login_config_id

fields.description: Facebook Login for Business configuration the Facebook button Connect opens. Meta takes the permissions and the asset picker (Pages and Instagram accounts) from it; when empty, Connect asks for the default permission list instead.

fields.name: graph_version
fields.label: Graph API Version (optional)
fields.hint: e.g. v23.0; default v23.0
fields.description: Facebook Graph API version every call is pinned to.

fields.name: webhook_verify_token
fields.label: Webhook verify token
fields.hint: Any long random string you choose. Paste the same value in Meta for Developers → your app → Webhooks (Instagram and Page objects) → Verify token, with the callback URL https://<server>/social/webhooks/meta
fields.description: Proves to Meta that the webhook URL is ours when Meta checks the subscription. Webhooks deliver Instagram and Messenger DMs and comments to the Inbox within seconds; the scheduled sync stays as the fallback.

SOCIAL_THREADS.label: Threads app
SOCIAL_THREADS.description: Connect Threads accounts; read posts and replies; publish threads

fields.name: app_id
fields.label: Threads App ID
fields.hint: developers.facebook.com/apps → your Threads app → Use cases → Threads API → Settings → Threads App ID (differs from the Meta App ID). Add the server callback URL shown on the settings page under Redirect Callback URLs there
fields.description: Threads app accounts are connected through.

fields.name: app_secret
fields.label: Threads App Secret
fields.hint: Same page → Threads App Secret
fields.description: Exchanges and refreshes Threads tokens.

fields.name: graph_version
fields.label: Threads API Version (optional)
fields.hint: e.g. v1.0; default v1.0
fields.description: Threads API version every call is pinned to.

SOCIAL_YOUTUBE.label: YouTube app
SOCIAL_YOUTUBE.description: Connect YouTube channels; read videos and comments; upload videos

fields.name: client_id
fields.label: YouTube (Google) OAuth Client ID
fields.hint: console.cloud.google.com → Credentials → OAuth client (Web). Enable the YouTube Data API v3 on the project
fields.description: Google OAuth client YouTube channels are connected through.

fields.name: client_secret
fields.label: YouTube (Google) OAuth Client Secret
fields.hint: GOCSPX-…
fields.description: Exchanges and refreshes YouTube tokens.

SOCIAL_LINKEDIN.label: LinkedIn app
SOCIAL_LINKEDIN.description: Connect LinkedIn Pages; read posts and comments; publish posts

fields.name: client_id
fields.label: LinkedIn Client ID
fields.hint: linkedin.com/developers/apps → your app → Auth. Needs the Community Management API product (read and post as company Pages)
fields.description: LinkedIn app company Pages are connected through.

fields.name: client_secret
fields.label: LinkedIn Client Secret
fields.hint: Same Auth tab, beside the Client ID
fields.description: Exchanges and refreshes LinkedIn tokens.

fields.name: api_version
fields.label: LinkedIn API Version (optional)
fields.hint: YYYYMM, e.g. 202509 — LinkedIn retires a version after a year; default 202509
fields.description: LinkedIn API version (YYYYMM) every call is pinned to.

SOCIAL_X.label: X app
SOCIAL_X.description: Connect X profiles; read posts and replies; publish posts

fields.name: client_id
fields.label: X OAuth 2.0 Client ID
fields.hint: developer.x.com → your project app → Keys and tokens → OAuth 2.0 Client ID. User authentication: Read and write, Type of App: Web App (confidential client)
fields.description: X OAuth 2.0 client profiles are connected through.

fields.name: client_secret
fields.label: X OAuth 2.0 Client Secret
fields.hint: Shown once, beside the Client ID
fields.description: Exchanges and refreshes X tokens.

fields.name: android_client_id
fields.label: Android Client ID (OAuth SDK)
fields.hint: Truecaller SDK console → your Android app → Client ID. Register package com.duncit.mobile with the release SHA-1
fields.description: Truecaller OAuth client the Android app offers one-tap phone sign-in with; served through publicClientConfig.

fields.name: app_key
fields.label: App Key (iOS + mobile web)
fields.hint: Truecaller SDK console → your iOS app / web app → App Key (partner key)
fields.description: Partner key the iOS app and mobile web use for Truecaller sign-in.

fields.name: ios_app_link
fields.label: iOS App Link
fields.hint: The universal link Truecaller gives the iOS app, e.g. https://si1a2b3c4d5e.truecallerdevs.com
fields.description: Universal link Truecaller returns the iOS app on.

fields.name: partner_name
fields.label: Partner name (mobile web)
fields.hint: The name Truecaller shows on the mobile-web consent sheet, e.g. Duncit. Set the web Callback URL to <server URL>/truecaller/callback
fields.description: Name the mobile-web Truecaller consent sheet shows.

fields.name: region
fields.label: Region
fields.hint: noneu (India and the rest of the world) or eu — blank means noneu
fields.description: Truecaller data region the server verifies proofs against (noneu or eu).

SERPER.label: Serper (Google search)
SERPER.description: Google search results for Marketing research and lead discovery

fields.name: api_key
fields.label: API Key
fields.hint: serper.dev → API Key (40 hex characters)
fields.description: Google search results for Marketing research and Instagram lead discovery.

ANTHROPIC.label: Anthropic (Claude)
ANTHROPIC.description: Claude models behind Reel Studio and the marketing agents

fields.name: api_key
fields.label: API Key
fields.hint: console.anthropic.com → API keys (sk-ant-…)
fields.description: Authenticates the Claude models Reel Studio and the marketing agents reason with.

fields.name: model
fields.label: Default model (optional)
fields.hint: e.g. claude-opus-5-5; a prompt in the AI Library may name its own
fields.description: Default Claude model when a prompt names none.

REMOTION.label: Remotion (Reel Studio licence)
REMOTION.description: The licence Reel Studio renders videos under

fields.name: license_key
fields.label: Company Licence Key
fields.hint: remotion.pro → your licence → the key. No entry at all is fine: Reel Studio still previews and exports, and Remotion prints its licence notice instead
fields.description: Reports Marketing → Reel Studio renders against the company licence. Remotion passes it in client code, so it is public by design and is served through publicClientConfig.

MONGODB.label: MongoDB (Duncit Intel)
MONGODB.description: Database connections Duncit Intel may read — and, with approval, write

fields.name: uri
fields.label: Connection URI
fields.hint: mongodb://user:password@host:27017/?authSource=admin
fields.description: Connects Duncit Intel to this database. Use a dedicated user: read-only for read connections, least privilege for write ones.

fields.name: database
fields.label: Default Database (optional)
fields.hint: e.g. duncit — Intel can override it per connection
fields.description: The database a connection reads when Intel names none.

MCP_SERVER.label: MCP server (Duncit Intel)
MCP_SERVER.description: Model Context Protocol servers Duncit Intel can call tools on

fields.name: url
fields.label: Server URL
fields.hint: https://mcp.duncit.com/mcp
fields.description: The Streamable HTTP endpoint Intel calls. HTTPS only; its host must also be on Intel › Settings › Security › MCP hosts.

fields.name: auth_token
fields.label: Access Token
fields.hint: A bearer token issued by the MCP server
fields.description: Authenticates Intel to the MCP server; tools run with this token holder's permissions.

fields.name: header_name
fields.label: Auth Header (optional)
fields.hint: Default Authorization (sent as Bearer)
fields.description: For servers that expect the token in another header, e.g. X-API-Key.

fields.name: client_id
fields.label: OAuth Client ID
fields.hint: xxxx.apps.googleusercontent.com
fields.description: The Google OAuth client the refresh token was issued to.

fields.name: client_secret
fields.label: OAuth Client Secret
fields.hint: GOCSPX-…
fields.description: Exchanges the refresh token for short-lived access tokens.

fields.name: refresh_token
fields.label: Refresh Token
fields.hint: 1//0… issued with the gmail.readonly scope
fields.description: Lets Intel read this mailbox without a password; revoke it in the Google account to cut access.

fields.name: mailbox
fields.label: Mailbox (optional)
fields.hint: team@duncit.com
fields.description: The address shown in Intel for this mailbox.

APPLE_WALLET.label: Apple Wallet (pod tickets)
APPLE_WALLET.description: Signs the .pkpass behind "Add to Apple Wallet"

fields.name: certificate
fields.label: Pass Type ID Certificate (PEM)
fields.hint: Identifiers → Pass Type IDs → e.g. pass.com.duncit.ticket → Create Certificate. Export it from Keychain as .p12, then `openssl pkcs12 -in pass.p12 -clcerts -nokeys -legacy` and paste the BEGIN CERTIFICATE block. The Pass Type ID and Team ID are read from it
fields.description: Pass Type ID certificate that signs every ticket pass; its subject names the pass type and the Apple team, so neither is typed separately.

fields.name: private_key
fields.label: Certificate Private Key (PEM)
fields.hint: `openssl pkcs12 -in pass.p12 -nocerts -legacy` — paste the whole BEGIN … PRIVATE KEY block
fields.description: Private key of the Pass Type ID certificate; signs the pass manifest.

fields.name: private_key_passphrase
fields.label: Private Key Passphrase (optional)
fields.hint: Only when the key above is ENCRYPTED (BEGIN ENCRYPTED PRIVATE KEY); blank for a plain key
fields.description: Unlocks an encrypted private key; blank when the key is stored unencrypted.

fields.name: wwdr_certificate
fields.label: Apple WWDR Certificate (PEM)
fields.hint: apple.com/certificateauthority → Worldwide Developer Relations - G4 (.cer), then `openssl x509 -inform der -in AppleWWDRCAG4.cer` and paste the BEGIN CERTIFICATE block
fields.description: Apple intermediate certificate that Wallet needs in the signature chain to trust the pass.

GOOGLE_WALLET.label: Google Wallet (pod tickets)
GOOGLE_WALLET.description: Signs the "Add to Google Wallet" save link

fields.name: issuer_id
fields.label: Issuer ID
fields.hint: Google Pay & Wallet Console → Google Wallet API → Issuer ID, a long number e.g. 3388000000022212345
fields.description: Issuer account that owns every ticket class and pass; prefixes their ids.

fields.name: service_account_json
fields.label: Service Account Key (JSON)
fields.hint: Paste the whole JSON key of a service account on a project with the Google Wallet API enabled, and add its client_email under Users in the Wallet console with Developer access
fields.description: Signs the save-to-wallet link (a JWT) so Google accepts the pass as issued by Duncit.

MONGO_URI.label: Production MongoDB URI
MONGO_URI.description: Written into the production server.env; the staging stack also reads it as the Data Clone source.
MONGO_URI.whyNotTechPortal: The server reads the Tech portal from its database, so a value it needs to reach that database (or to boot at all) cannot live there.

STAGING_MONGO_URI.label: Staging MongoDB URI
STAGING_MONGO_URI.description: Written into the staging server.env as its database.
STAGING_MONGO_URI.whyNotTechPortal: The server reads the Tech portal from its database, so a value it needs to reach that database (or to boot at all) cannot live there.

JWT_SECRET.label: Production JWT secret
JWT_SECRET.description: Signs and verifies every production sign-in token.
JWT_SECRET.whyNotTechPortal: The server reads the Tech portal from its database, so a value it needs to reach that database (or to boot at all) cannot live there.

STAGING_JWT_SECRET.label: Staging JWT secret
STAGING_JWT_SECRET.description: Signs staging sign-in tokens. Unset, staging falls back to JWT_SECRET and a staging token is valid on production, so it must be set.
STAGING_JWT_SECRET.whyNotTechPortal: The server reads the Tech portal from its database, so a value it needs to reach that database (or to boot at all) cannot live there.

SOCIAL_TOKEN_KEY.label: Social token sealing key
SOCIAL_TOKEN_KEY.description: Encrypts the social-network tokens stored in the database (32 bytes, base64 or hex).
SOCIAL_TOKEN_KEY.whyNotTechPortal: An encryption key must not be stored in the database it protects.

STAGING_SOCIAL_TOKEN_KEY.label: Staging social token sealing key
STAGING_SOCIAL_TOKEN_KEY.description: Same as SOCIAL_TOKEN_KEY for the staging stack.
STAGING_SOCIAL_TOKEN_KEY.whyNotTechPortal: An encryption key must not be stored in the database it protects.

OPENWA_API_MASTER_KEY.label: OpenWA gateway master key
OPENWA_API_MASTER_KEY.description: Bootstraps the WhatsApp gateway container's API keys; the server uses it to call the gateway.
OPENWA_API_MASTER_KEY.whyNotTechPortal: Read by a container that has no access to the main database at boot.

STAGING_OPENWA_API_MASTER_KEY.label: Staging OpenWA gateway master key
STAGING_OPENWA_API_MASTER_KEY.description: Same as OPENWA_API_MASTER_KEY for the staging stack.
STAGING_OPENWA_API_MASTER_KEY.whyNotTechPortal: Read by a container that has no access to the main database at boot.

STAGING_SUPER_ADMIN_PASSWORD.label: Staging root admin password
STAGING_SUPER_ADMIN_PASSWORD.description: Password the staging root super admin is created with on a fresh database. Unset, the server falls back to a weak default.
STAGING_SUPER_ADMIN_PASSWORD.whyNotTechPortal: The server reads the Tech portal from its database, so a value it needs to reach that database (or to boot at all) cannot live there.

LITE_MONGO_URI.label: Duncit Lite MongoDB URI
LITE_MONGO_URI.description: Duncit Lite's own database; unset uses the main host with a separate database name.
LITE_MONGO_URI.whyNotTechPortal: Read by a container that has no access to the main database at boot.

STAGING_LITE_MONGO_URI.label: Staging Duncit Lite MongoDB URI
STAGING_LITE_MONGO_URI.description: Same as LITE_MONGO_URI for the staging stack.
STAGING_LITE_MONGO_URI.whyNotTechPortal: Read by a container that has no access to the main database at boot.

LITE_JWT_SECRET.label: Duncit Lite JWT secret
LITE_JWT_SECRET.description: Signs Duncit Lite sign-in tokens; unset falls back to the main JWT secret.
LITE_JWT_SECRET.whyNotTechPortal: Read by a container that has no access to the main database at boot.

STAGING_LITE_JWT_SECRET.label: Staging Duncit Lite JWT secret
STAGING_LITE_JWT_SECRET.description: Same as LITE_JWT_SECRET for the staging stack.
STAGING_LITE_JWT_SECRET.whyNotTechPortal: Read by a container that has no access to the main database at boot.

LITE_MCP_SECRET.label: Duncit Lite MCP secret
LITE_MCP_SECRET.description: Shared by the API (signs) and Lite (verifies) for the MCP lite connector; unset is derived from the JWT secret.
LITE_MCP_SECRET.whyNotTechPortal: Read by a container that has no access to the main database at boot.

STAGING_LITE_MCP_SECRET.label: Staging Duncit Lite MCP secret
STAGING_LITE_MCP_SECRET.description: Same as LITE_MCP_SECRET for the staging stack.
STAGING_LITE_MCP_SECRET.whyNotTechPortal: Read by a container that has no access to the main database at boot.

DOCKERHUB_TOKEN.label: Docker Hub token

SSH_HOST.label: VPS host

DUNCIT_RELEASE_EMAIL.label: Release account email (optional)

DUNCIT_RELEASE_PASSWORD.label: Release account password (optional)

SONAR_HOST_URL.label: SonarQube URL (CI scan)

SONAR_TOKEN.whyNotTechPortal: Used by CI before or without a running Duncit server; fetching it from the portal would make CI depend on production being up.

CODECOV_TOKEN.label: Codecov token
CODECOV_TOKEN.whyNotTechPortal: Used by CI before or without a running Duncit server; fetching it from the portal would make CI depend on production being up.

EXPO_TOKEN.label: Expo token

EXPO_TOKEN.whyNotTechPortal: Used by CI before or without a running Duncit server; fetching it from the portal would make CI depend on production being up.

ANDROID_UPLOAD_STORE_PASSWORD.label: Android keystore password

ANDROID_UPLOAD_KEY_ALIAS.label: Android key alias

ANDROID_UPLOAD_KEY_PASSWORD.label: Android key password
ANDROID_UPLOAD_KEY_PASSWORD.whyNotTechPortal: Stays with the keystore it opens.

MWEB_ANDROID_CERT_SHA256.label: Android App Links fingerprints (transitional override)
